instruction:
Two-software CAE flow: SolidWorks -> Abaqus/CAE. No init file is provided; start from a new blank SolidWorks part.

Chain evidence requirement: use the design token EW_SW_ABQ_07. Keep this token encoded in the SolidWorks part/custom properties or STEP export metadata so the text of stage1_geometry.step contains EW_SW_ABQ_07 and SOLIDWORKS_TO_ABAQUS. In Abaqus/CAE, create at least one model, part, instance, set, surface, job description, or other native name containing both EW_SW_ABQ_07 and IMPORTED_FROM_stage1_geometry.step, so the final CAE file carries evidence that Abaqus consumed the SolidWorks STEP handoff.

1. In SolidWorks, use sketch and feature tools to create a 160 mm x 40 mm x 6 mm flat slotted link with one D14 eye hole near each end and a centered 60 mm x 12 mm through slot. Export the completed CAD geometry to C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage1_geometry.step.
2. In Abaqus/CAE, import stage1_geometry.step and create the finite-element model. Use the model name Model-SlottedLinkTension. Define material Steel with E=210000 MPa and nu=0.3, create a solid section using Steel, and assign it to the link. Create a Static General analysis step named Step-Tension. Create sets named LEFT_EYE, RIGHT_EYE, and SLOT_EDGE. Use a coarse first-order linear solid mesh with modest local seeding only around SLOT_EDGE; do not use quadratic elements. Create a boundary condition named BC-LeftEye that fixes LEFT_EYE. Create an action named Load-RightTension: either an approximately +1200 N axial tensile load on RIGHT_EYE, or an equivalent named axial displacement boundary condition on RIGHT_EYE. Submit the job named Job-SlottedLinkTension and wait for the analysis to complete.
3. Required deliverables on the Desktop: C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage1_geometry.step, C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-SlottedLinkTension.cae, and C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-SlottedLinkTension.odb. Do not create extra STEP, DXF, CAE, or ODB deliverables.

 First use SolidWorks to create and export the CAD STEP file, then use Abaqus/CAE to import that STEP file, build the finite-element model, submit the job, and save the CAE and ODB deliverables.
